questionText: Glucose pentaacetate does not react with hydroxylamine ($\text{NH}_2\text{OH}$) to form an oxime. What structural conclusion is drawn from this behavior?

options.text: Glucose pentaacetate possesses a linear keto-enol equilibrium
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: All five acetate groups are attached exclusively to the $C_1$ carbon atom
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: The anomeric $-OH$ at $C_1$ is locked as an acetate ester, preventing open-chain $-CHO$ regeneration
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT concept for Limitations of Open-Chain Structure Glucose Pentaacetate.

options.text: Hydroxylamine is rendered chemically inactive by acetate ions
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Biomolecules (Limitations of Open-Chain Structure Glucose Pentaacetate):
The anomeric $-OH$ at $C_1$ is locked as an acetate ester, preventing open-chain $-CHO$ regeneration

Detailed Context:
In glucose pentaacetate, the $-OH$ on the anomeric carbon ($C_1$) is converted into an acetate ester ($C_1-O-\text{COCH}_3$). Unlike the free hemiacetal $-OH$ of glucose, this acetal/ester group cannot readily open under mild conditions to regenerate a free aldehyde ($-CHO$) group. The absence of a free $-CHO$ group prevents oxime formation with $\text{NH}_2\text{OH}$, proving that glucose exists 

Therefore, option (C) is the correct answer.

questionText:
Read the passage carefully and answer the Questions
The term vitamin was coined from the word vital +amine since the earlier
identified compounds had amino groups. Later work showed that most of them
didn't contain amino groups. They are very essential for the body. They has to be
taken various diet or in the form of medicines also.
Vitamins are classified into two groups depending upon their solubility in water
or fat.
Fat soluble vitamins are soluble in fat and oils but insoluble in water. Thhey are
stored in liver and adipose (fat storing) tissues
Water-soluble vitamins are soluble in water. These must be supplied regularly in
diet because they are readily excreated in urine and cannot be stored in our
body.
What are the sources of Vitamin C?
